name: Jehiel
overview: Jehiel is a male biblical figure known primarily as the father of Obadiah, who accompanied Ezra during the return to Jerusalem. His tribal affiliation is not specified in Scripture. There are no additional notes recorded about him beyond this familial connection.
namesAndTitles: The name Jehiel means 'G-d [El] lives,' reflecting a theophoric element common in Hebrew names. This name is a proper name mentioned explicitly in Ezra 8:9, without indication that it was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Jehiel is identified as the father of Obadiah, who played a role in the return with Ezra. He is also noted as a descendant of Joab, establishing a lineage connection. Scripture does not provide further family details beyond these relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Jehiel's significance lies in his role as the progenitor of Obadiah, who was among those who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra, a pivotal moment in Israel's restoration. His descent from Joab connects him to a notable lineage, underscoring the continuity of God's people through generations. Although not a prominent figure himself, Jehiel's mention anchors the genealogical and communal identity of those involved in the post-exilic restoration.
